# 1.0 Introduction

Accessibility and service frequency are key issues in public transport. Previous research developed a Supply Index for census districts, which could be calculated in Melbourne using a database of bus, tram and train stations and routes provided by the public transport authority [@currie2007identifying]. However, this index was developed prior to the introduction of the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS), which provides a common, text-based format for the provision of transit timetable data.

A question, therefore, is how to calculate the Supply Index using GTFS data, and what related findings might be made. This document addresses this by using the statistical programming language R [@R-base], the tidytransit package [@tidytransit2023] and other tools to develop code to calculate the Supply Index. The GTFS files for Melbourne [@Transport:2023aa] are used as test data. 

The rest of this document is structured as follows: the next section discusses the research context of the Supply Index.  Section 3 explores the tidytransit package and the Melbourne GTFS file.  In Section 4 the Supply Index calculation is developed into R code. Section 5 presents results, followed by a brief discussion and conclusion in Section 6. 

# 2.0 Research context

The Supply Index^[![Supply Index formula](Supply_index.png)] was developed in @currie2007identifying. It uses thresholds for access at 400m for bus and tram stops, and 800m for railway stations.  These values are used in the calculation of the Area~Bn~ variable.The Area~CCD~ variable is based on the specific zone that is being examined^[In @currie2007identifying census districts were used.  Here the Australian Buraear of Statistics (ABS) Statistical Area 1 (SA1) zones will be used.].  The Service Level Measure (SL~Bn~) is the variable that needs to be extracted from the GTFS file.

# 3.2 Melbourne GTFS data 
Unfortunately, the Melbourne GTFS data does not appear to be directly downloadable by the tidytransit package^[This is because, rather than providing a single gtfs.zip file containing the various text files (e.g. stops.txt), the Melbourne GTFS file contains 10 directories, named 1-8, 10 and 11, each of which contains a gtfs.zip file for a single mode.]. Regardless, the Melbourne can be loaded manually with the read_gtfs tool provided in tidy transit.

Then the departure timetable code can be run, in this case dplyr::selecting Southern Cross Station and April 27, 2023^[Note, I've also converted the code from the tidytransit vignette into functions so that it can be run on any date, stop or time period.]. 

```{r departure_timetable_as_a_function, echo=FALSE, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, fig.cap="Melbourne, Southern Cross departure timetable for April 27, 2023", cache=TRUE}

#First turn the departure timetable code into a function
departure_timetable_function <- function(gtfs, stop_to_show, date_to_show){
  # get the id of the first stop in the trip's stop sequence
  first_stop_id <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
    group_by(trip_id) %>% 
    summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.min(stop_sequence)])

  # join with the stops table to get the stop_name
  first_stop_names <- left_join(first_stop_id, gtfs$stops, by="stop_id")

  # rename the first stop_name as trip_origin
  trip_origins <- first_stop_names %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_origin = stop_name)

  # join the trip origins back onto the trips
  gtfs$trips <- left_join(gtfs$trips, trip_origins, by = "trip_id")

  #gtfs$trips %>%
  #  dplyr::select(route_id, trip_origin) %>%
  #  head()

  if(!exists("trip_headsign", where = gtfs$trips)) {
    # get the last id of the trip's stop sequence
    trip_headsigns <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
      group_by(trip_id) %>% 
      summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.max(stop_sequence)]) %>% 
      left_join(gtfs$stops, by="stop_id") %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_headsign.computed = stop_name)

    # assign the headsign to the gtfs object 
    gtfs$trips <- left_join(gtfs$trips, trip_headsigns, by = "trip_id")
  }

  stop_ids <- gtfs$stops %>% 
    filter(stop_name == stop_to_show) %>% 
    dplyr::select(stop_id)

  departures <- stop_ids %>% 
    inner_join(gtfs$stop_times %>% 
                 dplyr::select(trip_id, arrival_time, 
                        departure_time, stop_id), 
               by = "stop_id")
  
  departures <- departures %>% 
    left_join(gtfs$trips %>% 
                dplyr::select(trip_id, route_id, 
                       service_id, trip_headsign, 
                       trip_origin), 
              by = "trip_id") 
  
  departures <- departures %>% 
    left_join(gtfs$routes %>% 
                dplyr::select(route_id, 
                       route_short_name), 
              by = "route_id")

  #departures %>% 
  #  dplyr::select(arrival_time,
  #         departure_time,
  #         trip_headsign,trip_origin,
  #         route_id) %>%
  #  head() %>%
  #  knitr::kable()

  #head(gtfs$.$dates_services)


  services_on_180823 <- gtfs$.$dates_services %>% 
    filter(date == date_to_show) %>% dplyr::select(service_id)

  departures_180823 <- departures %>% 
    inner_join(services_on_180823, by = "service_id")

#  departures_180823 %>%
 #   arrange(departure_time, stop_id, route_short_name) %>% 
  #  dplyr::select(departure_time, stop_id, route_short_name, trip_headsign) %>% 
   # filter(departure_time >= hms::hms(hours = 7)) %>% 
   # filter(departure_time < hms::hms(hours = 7, minutes = 10)) %>% 
  #  knitr::kable()

  route_colors <- gtfs$routes %>% dplyr::select(route_id, route_short_name, route_color)
  route_colors$route_color[which(route_colors$route_color == "")] <- "454545"
  route_colors <- setNames(paste0("#", route_colors$route_color), route_colors$route_short_name)

  output <- list(
      ggplot(departures_180823) + theme_bw() +
      geom_point(aes(y=trip_headsign, x=departure_time, color = route_short_name), size = 0.2) +
      scale_x_time(breaks = seq(0, max(as.numeric(departures$departure_time)), 3600), 
                   labels = scales::time_format("%H:%M")) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
      scale_color_manual(values = route_colors) 
  #    labs(title = paste("Departures from", stop_to_show, "on", date_to_show))
  #add a return value to provide the number of services shown in the graph as an output
          , nrow(departures_180823)
      )
  #return list with graph and the number of services. 
  return(output)
  
}
```

# 4.0 Supply Index calculation
There are three components to the Supply Index calculation: Area~Bn~ variable, Area~CCD~ and the Service Level Measure (SL~Bn~).  Functions for caluculating these are developed in the following. 

# 4.1 Service Level Measure

The code from the tidytransit vignette calculates the number of departures from a stop for a given day or part of a day.  Therefore, this code needs to be adjusted to perform similar calculations, but for arrivals rather than departures, and for a period of one week rather than one day.  


```{r arrival_timetable_as_a_function, echo=FALSE, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, fig.cap="Melbourne, Southern Cross arrival timetable for April 27, 2023", cache=TRUE}


#First turn the departure timetable code into a function
arrival_timetable_function <- function(gtfs, stop_to_show, date_to_show){
  # get the id of the first stop in the trip's stop sequence
  first_stop_id <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
    group_by(trip_id) %>% 
    summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.min(stop_sequence)])

  # join with the stops table to get the stop_name
  first_stop_names <- left_join(first_stop_id, gtfs$stops, by="stop_id")

  # rename the first stop_name as trip_origin
  trip_origins <- first_stop_names %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_origin = stop_name)

  # join the trip origins back onto the trips
  gtfs$trips <- left_join(gtfs$trips, trip_origins, by = "trip_id")

  
  #### get the id of the last stop in the trip's stop sequence
  last_stop_id <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
    group_by(trip_id) %>% 
    summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.max(stop_sequence)])

  # join with the stops table to get the stop_name
  last_stop_names <- left_join(last_stop_id, gtfs$stops, by="stop_id")

  # rename the last stop_name as trip_destination
  trip_destinations <- last_stop_names %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_destination = stop_name)

  # join the trip destinations back onto the trips
  gtfs$trips <- left_join(gtfs$trips, trip_destinations, by = "trip_id")

  
  #gtfs$trips %>%
  #  dplyr::select(route_id, trip_origin) %>%
  #  head()

  if(!exists("trip_headsign", where = gtfs$trips)) {
    # get the last id of the trip's stop sequence
    trip_headsigns <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
      group_by(trip_id) %>% 
      summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.max(stop_sequence)]) %>% 
      left_join(gtfs$stops, by="stop_id") %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_headsign.computed = stop_name)

  #create a new field with 
  trip_destination <- gtfs$stop_times %>% 
      group_by(trip_id) %>% 
      summarise(stop_id = stop_id[which.max(stop_sequence)]) %>% 
      left_join(gtfs$stops, by="stop_id") %>% dplyr::select(trip_id, trip_headsign.computed = stop_name)

    
    
    # assign the headsign to the gtfs object 
    gtfs$trips <- left_join(gtfs$trips, trip_headsigns, by = "trip_id")
  }

  stop_ids <- gtfs$stops %>% 
    filter(stop_name == stop_to_show) %>% 
    dplyr::select(stop_id)

  departures <- stop_ids %>% 
    inner_join(gtfs$stop_times %>% 
                 dplyr::select(trip_id, arrival_time, 
                        departure_time, stop_id), 
               by = "stop_id")
  
  departures <- departures %>% 
    left_join(gtfs$trips %>% 
                dplyr::select(trip_id, route_id, 
                       service_id, trip_headsign, 
                       trip_origin, 
                       trip_destination), 
              by = "trip_id") 
  
  departures <- departures %>% 
    left_join(gtfs$routes %>% 
                dplyr::select(route_id, 
                       route_short_name), 
              by = "route_id")

  #remove trips where first stop is equal to the stop_to_show, as these stops originate at this stop and so do not depart
  departures <- departures %>% 
      filter(trip_origin != stop_to_show)
  
  
  #departures %>% 
  #  dplyr::select(arrival_time,
  #         departure_time,
  #         trip_headsign,trip_origin,
  #         route_id) %>%
  #  head() %>%
  #  knitr::kable()

  #head(gtfs$.$dates_services)


  services_on_180823 <- gtfs$.$dates_services %>% 
    filter(date == date_to_show) %>% dplyr::select(service_id)

  departures_180823 <- departures %>% 
    inner_join(services_on_180823, by = "service_id")

#  departures_180823 %>%
 #   arrange(departure_time, stop_id, route_short_name) %>% 
  #  dplyr::select(departure_time, stop_id, route_short_name, trip_headsign) %>% 
   # filter(departure_time >= hms::hms(hours = 7)) %>% 
   # filter(departure_time < hms::hms(hours = 7, minutes = 10)) %>% 
  #  knitr::kable()

  route_colors <- gtfs$routes %>% dplyr::select(route_id, route_short_name, route_color)
  route_colors$route_color[which(route_colors$route_color == "")] <- "454545"
  route_colors <- setNames(paste0("#", route_colors$route_color), route_colors$route_short_name)

  #No need for list of outputs anymore, as the graphs are no longer needed
  #output <- list(
   #   ggplot(departures_180823) + theme_bw() +
    #  geom_point(aes(y=trip_origin, x=arrival_time, color = route_short_name), size = 0.2) +
     # scale_x_time(breaks = seq(0, max(as.numeric(departures$departure_time)), 3600), 
      #             labels = scales::time_format("%H:%M")) +
      #theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
      #theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
      #scale_color_manual(values = route_colors) 
  #    labs(title = paste("Departures from", stop_to_show, "on", date_to_show))
  #add a return value to provide the number of services shown in the graph as an output
       #   , nrow(departures_180823)
    #  )
  #return list with graph and the number of services. 
  return(departures_180823)
  
}
```

 Next, create a function that calculates the number of arrivals into a stop for a seven day period. 

```{r arrival_timetable_Swan_Hill_7_day, echo=FALSE, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, fig.cap="Swan Hill arrival timetable for week of April 27, 2023", cache=TRUE}

arrival_seven_day_function <- function(gtfs, stop_to_show, first_date){
  day1 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=first_date)
  day2 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 1))
  day3 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 2))
  day4 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 3))
  day5 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 4))
  day6 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 5))
  day7 <- arrival_timetable_function(gtfs=gtfs, stop_to_show=stop_to_show, date_to_show=(as.Date(first_date) + 6))
  
  week <- list(day1, day2, day3, day4, day5, day6, day7)
  
  return(week)

  }
```

# 4.2 Area~Bn~ variable 

As above, Area~Bn~ is 400m for bus and tram stops, and 800m for railway stations. Mode is described in the GTFS format using the 'route-type' variable in the 'route.txt' file as shown below^[Extract from GTFS routes specification [@GTFS_schedule_reference].]: ![GTFS mode codes](GTFS_mode_reference.png). 
This is not directly associated with the stop id, but as the Melbourne GTFS data is split up by mode anyway it should be possible to simply do the Area~Bn~ calculations individually for each stop and mode combination.  

# 4.3 Area~CCD~ variable
The Area~CCD~ variable is the square kilometre spatial area of the spatial zone that is under consideration. This number should be available from the source^[e.g. If using SA1 census areas, the land area is provided by the Australia Bureau of Statistics (ABS) together with the shape files.]. 

However, the complicating factor will be to figure out how much of each area associated with each stop is within which each spatial zone. However, there appear to be plenty of tools in R, including the sp package [@spatial_data_in_R, @applied_spatial_data_analysis_with_R] and an ABS data manipulation package called absmapsdata [@absmapsdata]^[See https://github.com/wfmackey/absmapsdata], which is used below to download and plot the latest Statistical Areas Level 1 files[@SA1_2021].



```{r load_abs_data, echo=FALSE, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, fig.cap="Melbourne SA1 map", cache=TRUE}

#Load SA1 data
sa1_map_data <- sa12021

#Map Greater Melbourne SA1 areas
map <- sa1_map_data %>%
  filter(gcc_name_2021 == "Greater Melbourne") %>%   # let's just look Melbourne
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(geometry = geometry,  # use the geometry variable
              fill = areasqkm_2021),     # fill by area size
          lwd = 0,                  # remove borders
          show.legend = TRUE) +    # keep legend
 # geom_point(aes(cent_long,
  #               cent_lat),        # use the centroid long (x) and lats (y)
   #          colour = "white") +    # make the points white
  theme_void() +                    # clears other plot elements
  coord_sf()

map

```


The GTFS files include stop locations in the stops.txt file, under the stop_lat and stop_long variables. The ABS map files store the boundaries as a dataframe in the geometry variable. The ptinpoly R package [@ptinpoly] appears to be the appropriate tool to figure out which stops are within which SA1 boundary. Running the example code^[Page 6-7, https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ptinpoly/ptinpoly.pdf]:

```{r ptinpoly_example, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="ptinpoly example code for pip2d function", cache=TRUE}
# Load sample data defining a comb, spiral, and fractal.
data(comb)
data(spiral)
data(fractal)

# Plot the comb, spiral, and fractal.
plot(rbind(comb,comb[1,]),type="l")
plot(rbind(spiral,spiral[1,]),type="l")
plot(rbind(fractal,fractal[1,]),type="l")

# Generate 3333 random test points.
set.seed(1902)
n <- 3333
x1 <- rnorm(n) ; x2 <- rnorm(n)
X <- cbind(x1,x2)
queries <- as.matrix(X)
# Check whether test points are contained in the comb, spiral, and factal.
# Most of these points will lie outside the polygons.
containment1 <- pip2d(comb,queries);
containment2 <- pip2d(spiral,queries);
containment3 <- pip2d(fractal,queries);

```

The output is interpreted as follows: ![pip2d output codes](pip2d_outputcodes.png).  Therefore, what is needed is to test each of the stop locations against each of the SA1 geometries, and then return the SA1 code or name for whichever SA1 the stop is in.  An example is provided here^[https://gis.stackexchange.com/a/343477], but I wasn't able to get that to work.  

But, in the meantime, I found this comment^[https://gis.stackexchange.com/a/261516], which references the ASGS R package [@ASGS_foyer]. However, the install function (install_ASGS()) does not appear to work.  

```{r ASGS_foyer, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="ptinpoly example code for pip2d function", cache=TRUE}
#See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ASGS.foyer/ASGS.foyer.pdf
#install_ASGS()


#Example
latlon2SA(-35.3, 149.2, to = "STE", yr = "2016")

#latlon2SA(-35.3, 149.2, to = "SA2", yr = "2016")



```

Next try this comment's^[https://gis.stackexchange.com/a/343479] code.



```{r sf_approach, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="ptinpoly example code for pip2d function", cache=TRUE}
#See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ASGS.foyer/ASGS.foyer.pdf
#install_ASGS()

pnts <- tibble(x = -34.92, y = 138.68)

library(sf)
# Shapefile from ABS: 
# https://www.abs.gov.au/AUSSTATS/abs@.nsf/DetailsPage/1270.0.55.004July%202016?OpenDocument
map = read_sf("data/SA1_2021.shp")

pnts_sf <- st_as_sf(pnts, coords = c('y', 'x'), crs = st_crs(map))

pnts <- pnts_sf %>% mutate(
  intersection = as.integer(st_intersects(geometry, map))
  , area = if_else(is.na(intersection), '', map$SA1_CODE21[intersection])
) 

pnts



```

That works.  The SA1 area code is returned in the area column.  Next step is to adjust this code so that it will report the SA1 area code for all stops in a GTFS file.  

```{r gtfs_SA1, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="ptinpoly example code for pip2d function", cache=TRUE}


map = read_sf("data/SA1_2021.shp")

add_2021_ABS_names_to_gtfs_stops_function <- function(gtfs){
  pnts <- tibble(stop_lat = gtfs$stops$stop_lat, stop_lon = gtfs$stops$stop_lon)
  pnts_sf <- st_as_sf(pnts, coords = c('stop_lon', 'stop_lat'), crs = st_crs(map))

  pnts <- pnts_sf %>% mutate(
    intersection = as.integer(st_intersects(geometry, map)), 
    area = if_else(is.na(intersection), '', map$SA1_CODE21[intersection])
  ) 
  gtfs$stops$SA1_CODE21 <- pnts$area
  gtfs$stops <- dplyr::left_join(gtfs$stops, map, by = "SA1_CODE21")
  return(gtfs$stops)
}

```


## 4.4 Putting the SI~CCD~ together
Next the areas (Area~Bn~ and Area~CCD~) and the Service Level Measure (SL~Bn~) are calculated for all of the SA1 areas at a single stop, added to a cumulative total field for each SA1 area, then repeated for all the stops. 

<!----

```{r stop_buffer_calc, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="Melbourne City, SI for week starting 27/04/23 for regional trains only", cache=TRUE}
library(raster)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

buffer_distance <- 800
gtfs <- mel1
start_date <- "2023-04-27"


# convert to sf format
dat_abs_sf <- sa1_map_data %>%
  # convert to simple features
  sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    st_transform(28355) # Reproject to EPSG:28355 as mentioned above

# Create SICCD variable for the running total.  Set units to square km for ease of calculation
dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- set_units(0, "km^2")


for (i in seq(1,nrow(gtfs$stops),1)) {
  #SI_CCD variable back to units of km^2
  dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- set_units(dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD, "km^2")
  
  dat_sim <- data.frame(lat = gtfs$stops$stop_lat[i],
                      long = gtfs$stops$stop_lon[i])

  # Convert to sf, set the crs to EPSG:4326 (lat/long), 
  # and transform to EPSG:28355 - as per https://epsg.io/28355
  dat_sf <- st_as_sf(dat_sim, coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>% 
  st_transform(28355)

  # Buffer circles by the buffer distance
  dat_circles <- st_buffer(dat_sf, dist = buffer_distance)

  
  # Intersect the circles with the polygons
  int_circles <- st_intersection(dat_abs_sf, dat_circles)

  # calculate Area Bn 
  int_circles$area_bn <- set_units(st_area(int_circles), "km^2") #Take care of units
  
  #Retrieve number of arrivals for day1-7
  SL_Bn <- arrival_seven_day_function(gtfs = gtfs, stop_to_show = gtfs$stops$stop_name[i], first_date = start_date)
  int_circles$SL_Bn <- nrow(SL_Bn[[1]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[2]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[3]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[4]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[5]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[6]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[7]])
  
  #Calculate SI_CCD for stop i
  int_circles$SI_CCD <- int_circles$area_bn / int_circles$areasqkm_2021 * int_circles$SL_Bn
  
  #Create ordinary tibble with SA1 code and SI_CCDs from stop i to add to the running totals
  export_to_ccds <- tibble(sa1_code_2021 = int_circles$sa1_code_2021, add_to_SI_CCD = int_circles$SI_CCD)

  #drop add_SI_CCD column from 
  dat_abs_sf <- dat_abs_sf[, !(colnames(dat_abs_sf) %in% "add_to_SI_CCD")]
  
  
  #merge based on sa1_code_2021
  dat_abs_sf <- left_join(dat_abs_sf, export_to_ccds)
  
  #SI_CCD and add_to_SI_CCD to non-unit numbers
  dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- as.vector(dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD)
  dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD <- as.vector(dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD)
  
  #replace NA with 0 
  dat_abs_sf[is.na(dat_abs_sf)] = 0
  
  #add the SI_CCDs for stop i to the running total of SI_CCD
  dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD + dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD
 
}
  


map <- dat_abs_sf %>%
  filter(sa3_name_2021 == "Melbourne City") %>%   # let's just look Melbourne
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(geometry = geometry,  # use the geometry variable
              fill = SI_CCD),     # fill by area size
          lwd = 0,                  # remove borders
          show.legend = TRUE) +    # keep legend
 # geom_point(aes(cent_long,
  #               cent_lat),        # use the centroid long (x) and lats (y)
   #          colour = "white") +    # make the points white
  theme_void() +                    # clears other plot elements
  coord_sf()

map



```


The SI~CCD~ for regional train services only within Melbourne City is as might be expected; the value is highest for the SA1 census districts closest to Southern Cross and Flinders Street station.

The next step generalises the code into a function that will calculate the SI~CCD~ for all SA1 districts, for any starting date, and using all of the relevant GTFS files for Victoria^[Not just the regional trains.].

```{r SICCD_calc_as_functions, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="SI for week starting 27/04/23 for Melbourne Metro trains, Melbourne City area", cache=TRUE}

##comment out to save memory
#buffer_distance <- 800
#gtfs <- mel1
#start_date <- "2023-04-27"
#EPSG_for_transform <- 28355

#sa1_map_data_vic <- sa1_map_data %>%
 # filter(state_name_2021 == "Victoria") # let's just look at Victoria




SICCD_calc_function <- function(sa1_map_data = sa1_map_data, gtfs = gtfs, start_date = start_date, EPSG_for_transform = EPSG_for_transform, buffer_distance = buffer_distance){

  # convert to sf format
  dat_abs_sf <- sa1_map_data %>%
    # convert to simple features
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
      st_transform(EPSG_for_transform) # Reproject to EPSG:28355 as mentioned above

  # Create SICCD variable for the running total.  Set units to square km for ease of calculation
  dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- set_units(0, "km^2")

  for (i in seq(1,nrow(gtfs$stops),1)) {
    #SI_CCD variable back to units of km^2
    dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- set_units(dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD, "km^2")
  
    dat_sim <- data.frame(lat = gtfs$stops$stop_lat[i],
                        long = gtfs$stops$stop_lon[i])

    # Convert to sf, set the crs to EPSG:4326 (lat/long), 
    # and transform to EPSG:28355 - as per https://epsg.io/28355
    dat_sf <- st_as_sf(dat_sim, coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>% 
    st_transform(EPSG_for_transform)

   # Buffer circles by the buffer distance
    dat_circles <- st_buffer(dat_sf, dist = buffer_distance)

    # Intersect the circles with the polygons
    int_circles <- st_intersection(dat_abs_sf, dat_circles)

    # calculate Area Bn 
    int_circles$area_bn <- set_units(st_area(int_circles), "km^2") #Take care of units
  
    #Retrieve number of arrivals for day1-7
    SL_Bn <- arrival_seven_day_function(gtfs = gtfs, stop_to_show = gtfs$stops$stop_name[i], first_date = start_date)
    int_circles$SL_Bn <- nrow(SL_Bn[[1]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[2]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[3]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[4]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[5]]) + 
      nrow(SL_Bn[[6]]) + nrow(SL_Bn[[7]]) 
    #Calculate SI_CCD for stop i
    int_circles$SI_CCD <- int_circles$area_bn / int_circles$areasqkm_2021 * int_circles$SL_Bn
  
    #Create ordinary tibble with SA1 code and SI_CCDs from stop i to add to the running totals
    export_to_ccds <- tibble(sa1_code_2021 = int_circles$sa1_code_2021, add_to_SI_CCD = int_circles$SI_CCD)

   #drop add_SI_CCD column from SA1 map
    dat_abs_sf <- dat_abs_sf[, !(colnames(dat_abs_sf) %in% "add_to_SI_CCD")]
  
  
    #merge based on sa1_code_2021
    dat_abs_sf <- left_join(dat_abs_sf, export_to_ccds)
  
    #SI_CCD and add_to_SI_CCD to non-unit numbers
    dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- as.vector(dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD)
    dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD <- as.vector(dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD)
  
    #replace NA with 0 
    dat_abs_sf[is.na(dat_abs_sf)] = 0
  
    #add the SI_CCDs for stop i to the running total of SI_CCD
    dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD <- dat_abs_sf$SI_CCD + dat_abs_sf$add_to_SI_CCD
 
  }
  return(dat_abs_sf)
}
```

Finally, the SICCD for each mode can be combined into a single dataframe, so that they can be added together. 


```{r SICCD_calc_mel_total <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- <- , echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="SI for week starting 27/04/23 for Skybus services, Melbourne City area", cache=TRUE}

mel_total_SICCD <- mel1_SICCD
colnames(mel_total_SICCD)[which(names(mel_total_SICCD) == "SI_CCD")]<-  "SI_CCD_regional_train"
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_metro_train <- mel2_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_tram <- mel3_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_bus <- mel4_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_regional_bus <- mel5_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_regional_bus_gippsland <- mel6_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_overland <- mel10_SICCD$SI_CCD
mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_skybus <- mel11_SICCD$SI_CCD

mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_total <- mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_regional_train + 
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_metro_train +
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_tram + 
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_bus +
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_regional_bus +
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_regional_bus_gippsland + 
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_overland + 
  mel_total_SICCD$SI_CCD_skybus


```

```{r ggmap, echo=FALSE, fig.margin=TRUE, fig.cap="maps generated from ggmap funciton", cache=TRUE}

qmap(baylor, zoom = 14)

ggmap(paris, extent = "normal")

ggmap(melbourne, extent = "normal")

melbourne_map
```
